summary: Marcus Bingenheimer specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Würzburg under Norbert Klaes, at Nagoya University, and under Huinan Yang. His posts include Dharma Drum Buddhist College, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, and Temple University.

Marek Mejor is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982), and served as a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under the supervision of Radek Chlup.

Margaret Dornish is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. She studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).
Margaret Gouin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret Mead was an anthropologist who studied at Barnard College and Columbia University. She spent her career primarily at the American Museum of Natural History (~1926–1978) and Columbia University (~1954–1978), also holding a post at the University of Rhode Island.

Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history. After studying at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union, she held faculty posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and Harvard University (attested 1999).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and completed postdoctoral work under Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya studied at St. Petersburg University, specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Central Asian studies. She was a longtime researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1956–2021) and held appointments at IRIAB and Soka University.
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her master's studies under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and also studied under Karin Preisendanz.

Maria Heim is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey. She has served as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Marianne Winder specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London and SOAS, and served as Keeper of the Oriental Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (~1964–1983) after a post at the University of Nottingham.
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania, where she studied under Sengaku Maeda.
Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 2006 under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He has held faculty posts at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and Rollins College.
Mario Kozah specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Cambridge under James Montgomery and held a post at the American University of Beirut.

Mario Poceski works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After completing his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he held positions at the University of Iowa and the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, having also studied under Robert A. Fowkes.

Mark A. Nathan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history. He earned his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and held appointments at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2010).

Mark Allon specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman, later working at SOAS (~1995–1999) and the University of Sydney (~2002).
